learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the secrets of human anatomy, how to capture action in stick figures, and the perfect proportions for drawing a realistic human body!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Artists use the length of the head as a standard unit of measurement. An average adult human figure is about 7.5 to 8 'heads' tall. A child's head is much larger in proportion to its body.
Quick, rough sketches that capture the action, movement, and pose of a figure, rather than the details. It helps in making the figure look alive and dynamic instead of stiff.
Start drawing humans with simple stick figures to get the pose right. Then, turn those sticks into cylinders, spheres, and blocks to give the body volume and 3D form.
When drawing a face (portrait), remember: the eyes are positioned exactly halfway between the top of the head and the chin. The space between the eyes is roughly the width of one eye.
When a figure is standing, its weight must be balanced. If a person is leaning, their center of gravity shifts. Capturing this balance is key to making the pose look realistic.

fun_activity.title: 🏃 Action Matchstick Men
fun_activity.instructions: Turn on a sports match or a dance video. Pause it at random moments and try to draw the pose of the athlete/dancer in just 10 seconds using ONLY stick figures. Focus on the angles of the spine, arms, and legs!

exam_tips: 📌 Always remember the standard proportion: an adult body is 7.5 to 8 heads tall.
📌 For facial proportions: The eyes sit exactly in the middle of the face horizontally.
📌 Gesture drawing is not about neatness; it is about capturing the energy and line of action.
quick_recap: ⭐ Understanding the basic skeletal structure helps in placing muscles correctly.
⭐ Block figures help artists understand the three-dimensional volume of the human body.
⭐ Drawing hands and feet requires breaking them down into simpler geometric shapes like wedges and boxes.
